sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: A PROGRESSIVE SHORTWAVE TROUGH OVER THE NRN PLAINS EMBEDDED WITHIN BELT OF STRONGER WLYS WILL ADVANCE THROUGH THE GREAT LAKES SATURDAY AND NERN STATES SATURDAY NIGHT. SMALLER SCALE VORTICITY MAXIMA INCLUDING MCV NOW LOCATED OVER SWRN MN WILL MOVE THROUGH THIS REGION AHEAD OF MAIN UPPER TROUGH. A QUASI-STATIONARY FRONT WILL STRETCH FROM THE NERN U.S. WWD TO A WEAK SURFACE LOW OVER THE UPPER GREAT LAKES EARLY SATURDAY. COLD FRONT WILL EXTEND SWWD FROM THIS LOW THROUGH IA AND WRN KS AND ADVANCE SWD...REACHING NRN OK LATER IN THE AFTERNOON.

sections.title: OH VALLEY...GREAT LAKES AND PORTIONS OF NERN STATES
sections.text: WARM ADVECTION STORMS NOW OVER SRN WI AND PROGRESSIVE MCS OVER MN AND IA WILL CONTINUE INTO THE GREAT LAKES EARLY SATURDAY. THE ATMOSPHERE WILL DESTABILIZE ACROSS SRN PORTIONS OF GREAT LAKES...OH VALLEY AND NERN U.S. SOUTH OF ONGOING ACTIVITY AS THE MOIST BOUNDARY LAYER WARMS WITH 2000-2500 J/KG MLCAPE EXPECTED. POTENTIAL WILL EXIST FOR STORMS TO INTENSIFY AND PRODUCE DAMAGING WIND AS THEY CONTINUE SEWD THROUGH LOWER MI. WEAK CAP AND DIABATIC WARMING WILL PROMOTE ADDITIONAL STORMS DEVELOPING ALONG RESIDUAL OUTFLOW BOUNDARIES AND LAKE BREEZES IN PRE-FRONTAL WARM SECTOR. WITH PRIMARY SURFACE LOW FORECAST TO DEVELOP INTO SERN CANADA...WIND PROFILES WILL REMAIN UNIDIRECTIONAL. A 50+ KT 500 MB JET MOVING THROUGH BASE OF UPPER TROUGH WILL CONTRIBUTE TO 30-40 KT BULK SHEAR SUPPORTIVE OF BOWING LINE SEGMENTS AND SUPERCELLS. DAMAGING WIND IS EXPECTED TO BE THE MAIN THREAT SINCE ANY HAIL THREAT WILL BE SOMEWHAT LIMITED BY WEAK MID-LEVEL LAPSE RATES. A COUPLE OF ISOLATED TORNADOES WILL ALSO BE POSSIBLE...MAINLY FROM SRN PARTS OF THE GREAT LAKES INTO EXTREME NRN PORTION OF THE OH VALLEY WHERE THE PROGRESSIVE WSWLY LOW LEVEL JET WILL AUGMENT 0-1 SHEAR. SEVERE THREAT SHOULD GRADUALLY DIMINISH BY

sections.title: KS THROUGH MO
sections.text: AMPLE DIABATIC WARMING OF THE MOIST BOUNDARY LAYER WITH DEWPOINTS IN THE 70S WILL RESULT IN 2500-3500 J/KG MLCAPE FROM CNTRL AND SRN KS EWD THROUGH MO. THUNDERSTORMS WILL LIKELY DEVELOP DURING THE AFTERNOON WITHIN ZONE OF CONVERGENCE ASSOCIATED WITH SEWD ADVANCING COLD FRONT. THIS REGION WILL REMAIN SOUTH OF THE STRONGER WLYS WITH WEAK VERTICAL SHEAR SUPPORTIVE OF MULTICELLS. HOWEVER...SOME OF THE STORMS COULD EVOLVE LINE SEGMENTS ALONG THE FRONT. ISOLATED WET DOWNBURSTS WILL BE PRIMARY THREAT. ANY SEVERE THREAT SHOULD DIMINISH RAPIDLY AFTER SUNSET.

sections.title: CNTRL WI
sections.text: DEWPOINTS IN THE 60S IN POST FRONTAL ZONE...COOLER AIR ALOFT AND FORCING FOR ASCENT ASSOCIATED WITH PROGRESSIVE SHORTWAVE TROUGH WILL CONTRIBUTE TO MODEST INSTABILITY AND LIKELIHOOD OF A FEW THUNDERSTORMS ACROSS WI DURING THE AFTERNOON. THE CONVECTIVE LAYER IS FORECAST TO BE RELATIVELY SHALLOW. HOWEVER...EFFECTIVE SHEAR OF 40+ KT WILL SUPPORT POTENTIAL FOR ORGANIZED STORMS WITH A THREAT OF STRONG GUSTY WINDS AND PERHAPS A TORNADO OR TWO. GIVEN POTENTIALLY MARGINAL THERMODYNAMIC ENVIRONMENT...WILL INTRODUCE LOW SEVERE PROBABILITIES AT THIS TIME. HOWEVER...AREA WILL BE MONITORED FOR A POSSIBLE SLIGHT RISK IN LATER OUTLOOKS. ..DIAL/SMITH.. 07/24/2010

sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: THE WLYS WILL REMAIN CONFINED TO THE NRN TIER OF STATES AS SUBTROPICAL RIDGE PERSISTS OVER THE SOUTHEAST...AND SEVERAL WEAK UPR LOWS/VORT CENTERS LINGER OVER THE SRN PLNS...THE SWRN STATES...AND OFF THE CA CST. FAIRLY STRONG SHORTWAVE IMPULSE THAT CROSSED THE NRN PLNS YESTERDAY WILL CONTINUE E ACROSS THE UPR GRT LKS TODAY...AND INTO SRN ONT/QUE EARLY SUN. S AND E OF THE TROUGH...SMALLER CONVECTIVELY-INDUCED VORT CENTERS/MC VS MAY CONTINUE TO FORM IN DEEP MOISTURE PLUME BOUNDING IMMEDIATE N AND W SIDES OF THE SUBTROPICAL RIDGE. AT THE SFC...COLD FRONT ATTENDANT TO GRT LKS IMPULSE WILL MOVE GENERALLY E/SE ACROSS THE UPR GRT LKS/MID MS VLY/CNTRL PLNS TODAY...AND SHOULD REACH THE TX PANHANDLE/NW OK BY LATE AFTN. THE FRONT MAY REMAIN SOMEWHAT ILL-DEFINED OVER WI AND MI FOR SOME TIME TODAY...UNTIL WEAK LOW NOW OVER WI IS ABSORBED WITHIN CONSOLIDATING WSWLY FLOW AHEAD OF UPR TROUGH. FARTHER E...DIFFUSE WARM FRONT SHOULD CONTINUE/NE ACROSS THE REMAINDER OF NEW ENGLAND BY EVE.

sections.title: IL/IND/LWR MI TO LWR GRT LKS/NERN STATES TODAY/TONIGHT
sections.text: STRONG DESTABILIZATION...WITH SBCAPE TO 3000 J/KG...SHOULD OCCUR TODAY ALONG SRN AND ERN FRINGE OF OVERNIGHT CONVECTIVE CLUSTERS ...I.E. FROM NRN/CNTRL IL ENE INTO SRN LWR MI...OH...AND WRN PA/NY. THIS SHOULD SUPPORT INTENSIFICATION OF RESIDUAL STORMS AND/OR DEVELOPMENT OF NEW ACTIVITY ALONG OUTFLOW BOUNDARIES AND LAKE BREEZE BOUNDARIES BY MID TO LATE AFTN. SEASONABLY STRONG...DEEP UNIDIRECTIONAL WSWLY WIND PROFILES ...WITH 40-50 KT 700-500 MB FLOW ON S SIDE OF UPR TROUGH...SHOULD SUPPORT BOWING LINE SEGMENTS AND SUPERCELLS...WITH DMGG WIND THE MAIN SVR THREAT. A COUPLE TORNADOES MAY ALSO OCCUR...MOST LIKELY OVER THE LWR GRT LKS...WHERE LOW LVL DIRECTIONAL SHEAR IS APT TO BE GREATEST. ALTHOUGH THE SVR THREAT SHOULD GRADUALLY DIMINISH THROUGH LATE EVE...A MORE LIMITED WIND DMG THREAT MAY PERSIST INTO EARLY SUN IN PA/NY AS APPROACHING UPR TROUGH ENHANCES LARGE SCALE FORCING FOR ASCENT.

sections.title: KS/MO AND NRN OK AFTN/EVE
sections.text: STRONG SFC HEATING OF VERY MOIST PREFRONTAL ENVIRONMENT SHOULD YIELD STRONG INSTABILITY /SBCAPE TO 3500 J PER KG/ FROM SRN/ERN KS INTO CNTRL/NRN MO LATER TODAY. TSTMS LIKELY WILL INTENSIFY/ DEVELOP IN WEAKLY CAPPED ENVIRONMENT BY MID AFTN ALONG/AHEAD OF AFOREMENTIONED COLD FRONT. WHILE REGION WILL LIE WELL S OF STRONGER FLOW ALOFT...GIVEN DEGREE OF INSTABILITY/LOW LVL UPLIFT...SUFFICIENT SHEAR WILL EXIST FOR SVR MULTICELLS AND PERHAPS A FEW MARGINAL SUPERCELLS. THESE WILL BE CAPABLE OF LOCALLY DMGG WIND AND SVR HAIL. ALTHOUGH THE SLOWLY-MOVING STORMS/CLUSTERS COULD LINGER INTO THE NIGHT...EVENTUALLY AFFECTING NRN OK AND POSING A RISK FOR HEAVY RAIN...ANY APPRECIABLE SVR THREAT SHOULD DIMINISH RAPIDLY WITH SUNSET.

sections.title: NRN/ERN MN SEWD INTO WI THIS AFTN
sections.text: UPR 50S TO LWR 60S F SFC DEWPOINTS WILL PERSIST IN POST-FRONTAL ENVIRONMENT OVER NE MN AND NRN/WRN WI. AT THE SAME TIME... SEASONABLY COOL AIR ALOFT AND FORCING FOR ASCENT WILL BE PRESENT JUST AHEAD OF UPR TROUGH. THIS SETUP MAY YIELD SCTD DIURNALLY ENHANCED TSTMS WITH A THREAT FOR HAIL. FARTHER SE...SOMEWHAT MORE SUBSTANTIAL MOISTURE WILL LINGER OVER CNTRL AND SRN/ERN WI...UNTIL COLD FRONT CONSOLIDATES AND ACCELERATES E INTO MI. AMPLE /40+ KT/ DEEP SHEAR WILL BE PRESENT FOR SUSTAINED STORMS/SUPERCELLS OVER THE REGION. THESE COULD POSE A THREAT FOR SVR WIND/HAIL AND POSSIBLY A TORNADO. HOWEVER ...LINGERING CLOUDS...OUTFLOW FROM OVERNIGHT CONVECTION...AND WEAK FRONTAL CONVERGENCE TOGETHER CAST DOUBT AS TO THE LIKELIHOOD FOR SUSTAINED STORMS. THUS...WILL MAINTAIN ONLY LOW SVR PROBABILITIES IN WI ATTM.

LITTLE CHANGE REQUIRED IN THE PREVIOUS OUTLOOK WHICH DISCUSSES THE EXPECTED SCENARIO IN DETAIL.

sections.title: FAR SERN NEB/FAR NERN KS/FAR NWRN MO
sections.text: REGIONAL RADAR IMAGERY SHOWED TSTMS CONTINUING TO DEVELOP IN A POST-FRONTAL ENVIRONMENT FROM FAR NERN KS/FAR SERN NEB INTO FAR NWRN MO. THIS ACTIVITY SHOULD REMAIN SLIGHTLY ELEVATED GIVEN THAT IT IS DEVELOPING N OF THE COLD FRONT. MODERATE INSTABILITY AND EFFECTIVE BULK SHEAR 30-40 KT SUGGESTS A POTENTIAL FOR SOME THREAT FOR HAIL AND STRONG WIND GUSTS. THUS...LOW SEVERE WIND AND HAIL PROBABILITIES HAVE BEEN EXPANDED NWD TO ACCOUNT FOR THIS SEVERE THREAT.

sections.title: PART OF NWRN/NORTH CENTRAL OK
sections.text: LOW SEVERE WIND AND HAIL PROBABILITIES HAVE BEEN EXPANDED SWD SOME ACROSS NWRN AND NORTH CENTRAL OK WHERE VISIBLE SATELLITE/REGIONAL RADAR IMAGERY AND LIGHTNING DATA INDICATED TSTMS DEVELOPING THIS AFTERNOON ALONG A WEAK PRE-FRONTAL SURFACE CONFLUENCE ZONE. SURFACE TEMPERATURE-DEWPOINT SPREADS TO AROUND 30 DEGREES SUGGEST STRONG WIND GUSTS WILL BE POSSIBLE.
